newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weaker as c. bank buys dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weaker as c. bank buys dlrs.

text.p: The Philippine peso slipped at the close on Wednesday after the central bank said it had started buying dollars again, traders said.
The peso ended at 29.30 to the dollar from the previous close of 29.

President Fidel Ramos said in a televised press conference the central bank bought $1 million from the market and sold $4 million in the morning. He did not specify the buying and selling rates during his afternoon news conference.
Since the central bank intervention was very limited, many traders were not aware of the dollar buying.
"Some would have thought that the buying rate must be at 29.00, prompting one bank to buy it up to 29.30," a trader said.
The central bank had been selling dollars at 29 pesos since Monday, after allowing the peso to float freely last Friday.
The foreign exchange market has been quiet since Monday as players opted to stay out of the market. Total turnover was light at $23.25 million, half of Tuesday's $46 million.
"People are not sure on how to trade the peso," another trader said.
They expected the peso to fluctuate within the 29.00 to 30.00 band in the coming days.-- Ramoncito dela Cruz (63 2) 841-8938
